newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish health board says E coli scare not epidemic.
newsitem.headline: Irish health board says E coli scare not epidemic.

text.p: Ireland's Eastern health board (EHB) said there is no evidence of an E Coli epidemic, following the death of a three-year-old girl in Dublin at the weekend.

"We are not dealing at the present time with an outbreak (of E coli) here," Dr. Brian O'Herlihy, EHB director of public health told Irish radio on Tuesday. "I can't rule out the possibility of one or two more cases but the longer it goes on without further cases the less likely it seems."
A three-year-old child died at the weekend in Dublin's Crumlin hospital from complications of an illness caused by the bacteria E coli.
O'Herlihy said ongoing investigations, following the death of the child, have so far proved negative.
The first case of E coli infection in Ireland was reported in two children in November 1995.
